source_tasks.problem: The expression $7 -  7 +  5 -  7 -  7 \cdot  5 \times  5$ may be changed only by inserting parentheses; rearranging numbers or operations is not allowed. In total, how many values can be obtained?

Consider the expression $6 \cdot  7 \cdot  7 +  2 -  6 -  3 -  8$. Fully parenthesize it in every possible way without changing the order of numbers or operations. Parenthesizations with the same numerical result count only once. How many distinct values are possible?

interface_note: Only parameter values vary; all mathematical conditions and requested quantity remain those stated by the supplied source questions. Names describe source data, not a target algorithm. Implement solve(parameters), no natural-language applicability detection. operators must have exactly len(operands)-1 entries.

observations: Both source questions fix an ordered sequence of operands and binary operators (+,-,*) and allow only full parenthesization (no reordering).
The requested quantity is the number of distinct numerical values over all full binary parenthesizations of the fixed expression.
The interface supplies operands (integers) and operators (length = len(operands)-1), so the procedure can be parameterized directly.
Distinct values must be deduplicated exactly; integer arithmetic avoids floating-point issues.
The number of full parenthesizations grows Catalan-like, so a DP over intervals with sets of achievable values is appropriate for up to 8 operands.
analysis.procedure_plan: Implement solve(parameters): read operands a[0..n-1] and operators op[0..n-2]. If n==1 return 1 (single value). Use interval DP: for each i<=j compute set S[i][j] of all values obtainable by fully parenthesizing a[i..j] with op[i..j-1]. Base S[i][i]={a[i]}. For length L=2..n, for each i, j=i+L-1, for each split k in [i, j-1], combine every x in S[i][k] and y in S[k+1][j] using op[k] (+,-,*) and insert into S[i][j]. Return the cardinality of S[0][n-1]. Use exact integer arithmetic and hash sets for deduplication.
analysis.uncertainty: The plan assumes the intended quantity is exactly the count of distinct values from full parenthesizations preserving operand/operator order, which matches both source statements. If the source intended a different counting convention (e.g., counting parenthesizations rather than distinct values), the DP would need modification; no such ambiguity is evident from the supplied text.
